cards.text: Abraham and Sarah have been waiting on a son. The LORD told Abraham that Sarah would have one, and Sarah, listening at the tent entrance, laughed to herself (Genesis 18:10-12). Now, friend, the LORD attends to Sarah, and she conceives.

cards.question: The LORD once said Sarah's son would come at a set time (Genesis 18:14). When does Sarah's son arrive?

answers.text: At the very time God had promised
A full year after the promised time
Many years after the promised time

cards.text: Sarah bears Abraham a son in his old age, right on God's schedule. Friend, I set a timer for ten minutes, walk away, and come back to a tray of CHARCOAL.

cards.question: The LORD does for Sarah what He had promised.

cards.text: Now this baby needs a name. And Abraham's the one picking it, no group chat vote, no list of forty options taped to the fridge.

cards.question: Abraham gives the name ___ to the son Sarah bore him.

cards.text: God had told Abraham that every boy among his people must be circumcised at eight days old (Genesis 17:12). And now, friend, there's a brand-new baby boy in the tent.

cards.question: Abraham waits until Isaac is a year old to circumcise him.
Abraham was ___ years old when his son Isaac was born to him.

cards.text: Then Sarah says God has made her laugh. I bet the last time she laughed it was the 'yeah, right' kind, but THIS laugh? Whole different recipe.

cards.question: Sarah says God has made her laugh. Who does she say will laugh with her?

cards.text: Sarah adds that nobody would have told Abraham she'd ever nurse children, yet she's borne him a son. No neighbor and no group chat would've dared send THAT text.
The child grows and gets weaned. And Abraham marks the day.

cards.question: How does Abraham mark the day Isaac is weaned?

answers.text: He offers a sacrifice at Bethel

cards.text: Quick reminder: Hagar is Sarah's Egyptian maidservant, and she bore Abraham a son named Ishmael (Genesis 16:1, 15). Now Sarah sees what Hagar's son is doing to her son Isaac.

cards.question: What does Sarah see Hagar's son doing to Isaac?
Sarah goes to Abraham and tells him to send Hagar and her son away.
Sarah says the slave woman's son will never share in the ___ with her son Isaac.

cards.text: This hits Abraham hard: the matter distresses him greatly, because it concerns his son Ishmael. Friend, this isn't some squabble over who ate the last cookie, this is his BOY.
Then God speaks to Abraham: "Do not be distressed about the boy and your maidservant." Friend, when you're tied up in knots, THAT is the voice you want to hear.

cards.question: God tells Abraham to listen to everything Sarah tells him. What reason does God give?

answers.text: His offspring will be counted through Isaac
His offspring will be counted through Ishmael
Hagar will find a better home in Egypt

cards.question: God tells Abraham that nothing will come of the slave woman's son.

cards.text: Early in the morning, Abraham gets up and puts bread and a skin of water on Hagar's shoulders. Then he sends her away with the boy, and I bet that goodbye sat heavy on him, friend.

cards.question: Hagar leaves and wanders. In which wilderness?

cards.text: Then the water in the skin is gone. Hagar leaves the boy under one of the bushes, and friend, that's about as low as a moment gets.

cards.question: Hagar goes and sits down about a bowshot away from the boy. Why does she say she's sitting that far off?

answers.text: She cannot bear to watch him die
She wants to search for water
She wants to pray by herself

cards.text: As she sits there, Hagar lifts up her voice and weeps. Then, friend, a voice comes down from heaven itself: the angel of God calls to her, "What is wrong, Hagar?" and tells her not to be afraid.

cards.question: The angel tells Hagar that God has heard the voice of the boy.
The angel tells Hagar to get up and take the boy by the hand, because God will make him into a great ___.
Then God opens Hagar's eyes. What does she see?

cards.text: She goes, fills the skin with water and gives the boy a drink. I know a little something about thinking it's all over in the dark, friend, and then the light shows up.

cards.question: God is with the boy, and he grows up in the wilderness and becomes a great ___.
While Ishmael is living in the Wilderness of Paran, his mother gets him a wife from the land of ___.

cards.text: And that's where we'll leave it for now, friend. Abraham's story still has PLENTY of time left on the timer.

findings.problem: The earlier cards have already established this answer: card 1 says the LORD attends to Sarah after promising a son, and card 3 says she bears the son right on God's schedule. This leaves nothing new for the baker to work out when asked whether the LORD did what He had promised.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: The setup says only that Abraham is choosing the baby's name. Nothing in the earlier cards supplies Isaac's name or a clue from which to infer it, so Jacob and Joseph are just as plausible to a baker who does not already know the passage.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The earlier cards establish only that Abraham is old. Sixty, eighty and a hundred all fit that description, and no setup gives the baker a reasoned way to choose his exact age.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The preceding cards establish mocking and Sarah's demand for expulsion, but they say nothing about inheritance or otherwise set up that concern. The baker is asked to supply an unseen word rather than reason out a meaning from the setup.

findings.problem: Inheritance is an abstract legal share, while tent and camp are physical places. It is also the only answer that naturally completes the phrase share in the, so the correct answer stands out and the two alternatives are not believable completions of Sarah's statement.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: No earlier card positively tells the baker what God intends to make of Ishmael. Card 8 merely rules out the statement that nothing will come of him, leaving no basis for reasoning that nation, rather than army or city, completes this promise.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: Nothing in the earlier cards points toward archery. Growing up in the wilderness does not make archer clearly more inferable than shepherd, so the baker must guess the unseen wording of verse 20.

findings.problem: The question never identifies the boy as Ishmael or connects him to Hagar. The boy and he depend on cards that are no longer visible rather than giving the needed context within the question itself.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what.
